concepts.why: The patient presents with muffled heart sounds, mediastinal widening, and a large pericardial effusion, which are all indicative of pericarditis.
The patient has an anterior mediastinal mass, which is a type of tumor that can cause mediastinal widening and pericardial effusion.
The patient presents with pleuritic chest pain and decreased breath sounds at the right lower zone, which are indicative of pleurisy.
The patient has a history of intermittent fever over the preceding 3 months, which is indicative of fever of unknown origin.

rationales.F01: Dyspnea can be associated with pericarditis and pleurisy.
rationales.F02: Pleuritic chest pain is a common symptom of pericarditis and pleurisy.
rationales.F07: Muffled heart sounds are a classic sign of pericardial effusion, often seen in pericarditis.
rationales.F10: Electrical alternans is a specific ECG finding associated with pericardial effusion, which is often seen in pericarditis.
rationales.F11: A large pericardial effusion is a key finding in pericarditis.
rationales.F12: An anterior mediastinal mass can be associated with various conditions, including mediastinal tumors.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of an anterior mediastinal mass on contrast-enhanced thoracic CT, along with mediastinal widening on chest radiograph, strongly supports the diagnosis of a mediastinal tumor, which can also explain the associated pericardial and pleural effusions.
